verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 8, 11, 12 show a flat concrete terrace with dark waterproofed screed surface, solid RCC parapet walls and RCC headroom; no slope, tiles or sheets.
verdicts.rationale: Flat RCC terrace clearly visible in multiple roof photos; matches 'RCC Flat Roof'.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The solar water heater, ladder, are the obstructions that could affect the solar installation.
verdicts.photo_observation: Evacuated-tube solar water heater with tank (pp. 6, 8, 10-12) and steel ladders to headroom/upper roof (pp. 6, 8, 19) are visible. Also visible but not listed: headroom/water-tank structure, a glass skylight (p.13) and potted plants on the lower terrace.
verdicts.rationale: Both named obstructions are clearly present; additional minor items (headroom, skylight) are consistent with the layout and do not contradict the answer.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: No installed panels exist; only SketchUp renders (pp. 23-24) show a low-tilt elevated array. Tilt cannot be measured from renders or roof photos.
verdicts.rationale: Renders are consistent with a shallow tilt but give no measurable angle; 7° cannot be verified visually.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Layout (pp. 23-24) shows two sub-arrays (6 modules along the long parapet, 2 modules on the short side parapet) both on the same top-floor RCC roof; 'Proposed PV Area' photos (p.11) mark the same terrace parapets.
verdicts.rationale: Both sub-arrays sit on a single roof; 8 modules total matches the 4.96 kWp (8 x 620 Wp) system.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?
verdicts.photo_observation: Renders (pp. 23-24) show modules on raised legs mounted over/along the parapet walls, cantilevering beyond the roof edge; p.11 photos mark the parapet tops as the PV area. Observations note MS fabrication under customer scope.
verdicts.rationale: Elevated structure is clearly depicted in the layout; rail type (AL short rail) is not visually verifiable but nothing contradicts it.

verdicts.question: What is the orientation of the solar panels?
verdicts.photo_observation: Top view (p.23) has north arrow pointing up; the main 6-module array sits along the NORTH parapet edge and a 2-module array on the EAST side. Solar water heater tubes slope toward the south. Tilt direction of the modules is not readable from the renders.
verdicts.rationale: Array placement on the north/east edges does not by itself contradict a south-facing tilt, but the renders do not clearly show which way the modules tilt; verify in design file.

verdicts.question: How can the roof be accessed?
verdicts.photo_observation: Internal staircase (pp. 7, 9) reaches the 2nd-floor utility/terrace level; from that terrace a steep steel ladder (p.8 top, blue route) climbs to the upper RCC roof where the PV area and water heater are. A second fixed ladder leads to the headroom top (pp. 6, 19).
verdicts.rationale: Final access to the PV roof is by ladder, consistent with the answer (staircase covers the lower part of the route).

verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior photos (pp. 5, 25) show a fully finished, painted building with glazing, grilles, gate and landscaping; interior utility room is occupied (washing machine, AC unit).
verdicts.rationale: Clearly a completed, occupied building.

verdicts.question: In an under-construction building, are existing conduit pipes available for AC, DC cables, and earthing?
verdicts.photo_observation: Building is complete; cable routes (pp. 12-18) are drawn along external walls/downpipes and a new wall hole is proposed (p.15), implying no pre-laid conduits.
verdicts.rationale: Consistent with no existing conduits; question is largely moot as the building is not under construction.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.designer_answer: The height of the building is G+2+headroom is approximately 15 meters
verdicts.photo_observation: Building exterior (pp. 5, 25): ground/stilt level with gate and parking, two upper residential floors with balconies, plus headroom with steel railing visible at top.
verdicts.rationale: G+2+headroom clearly visible; ~15 m height is plausible though not measurable from the photo (typical G+2+headroom is ~12-14 m).

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior photo (pp. 5, 25) shows a G+2+headroom residential building; roof photos match the 3D layout (water heater, ladder, headroom, skylight).
verdicts.rationale: Photos and layout are mutually consistent with the description.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Building exterior (pp. 5, 25) shows a utility pole directly in front of the building with multiple overhead conductors running within ~1-3 m of the front facade and balconies; p.5 bottom also shows street wires. Conductor voltage class (LT vs 11 kV HT) cannot be determined from the photo.
verdicts.rationale: Overhead lines are definitely within 10 m; they look like LT distribution but HT cannot be ruled out visually. Confirm voltage class and safe lifting clearance (lifting route on p.5 is on the facade near these wires).

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.5 shows a paved residential street directly in front of the gated compound; p.5 bottom (view from roof) shows the road adjacent to the building.
verdicts.rationale: Paved road access up to the gate is clearly visible.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.designer_answer: details: The existing chajja are the obstacles that could hinder the material lifting.
verdicts.photo_observation: p.5 facade shows projecting chajjas/sunshades over windows and a glass-railed balcony; lifting route drawn up the right side of the facade. Overhead wires near the front of the building are also visible.
verdicts.rationale: Chajjas are clearly visible along the lift path. Note: overhead wires near the facade are an additional lifting hazard not mentioned.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: The Inverter, ACDB, DCDB, Battery will be installed near the headroom which is near the terrace.
verdicts.photo_observation: pp. 14 and 21 show overlays of Inverter/ACDB/DCDB and Battery on a plain wall in the top-floor utility room (washing machine, LG AC indoor unit), which opens onto the terrace (p.7 bottom, p.8 top).
verdicts.rationale: Equipment location is on the top floor adjacent to the terrace, consistent with the answer.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Equipment wall (pp. 14, 21) is inside a roofed utility room, protected from rain and direct sun.
verdicts.rationale: Indoor/sheltered location; no canopy needed.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_answer: The earth pits are located near the ground floor which is near to the garden area.
verdicts.photo_observation: p.22 'Earth Pit Location' marks LA pit, DC and AC earth pits in a soil planter strip along the ground-level compound wall with potted/garden plants.
verdicts.rationale: Pits are at ground level in a garden strip exactly as described.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.photo_observation: No photo of the router or its location is included.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?

verdicts.question: Is the Termination Point easily visible or sealed?

verdicts.question: Is a Lightning Arrestor (LA) already available at the site?

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.9: right side of meter board is occupied by three fuse carriers. p.21 overlay places the Solar Meter over the fuse-carrier area with caption 'Client will relocate the fuses for placing solar meter'.
verdicts.rationale: Space exists only after the customer relocates the fuses - consistent with the designer's note (customer scope). Answer is conditional, not unconditionally 'Yes'.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.22 shows an open soil planter strip along the compound wall with LA, DC and AC pit positions marked; p.18 shows the same strip.
verdicts.rationale: Exposed soil area with room for three pits is visible (some pots may need shifting).

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is an LA extension provided at the far end?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.19 shows a single LA on the headroom railing; layout renders (pp. 23-24) show no LA extension at the array's far end. The 6-module array along the parapet is ~6.9 m long and extends away from the headroom.
verdicts.rationale: Photos are consistent with no extension, but LA coverage of the far end of the elevated/cantilevered array should be confirmed by design.

verdicts.question: In case of elevated structures, is it with or without grouting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Renders show structure legs on parapet/roof slab; no physical structure or grouting detail visible in site photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Layout (pp. 23-24) shows modules cantilevered beyond the parapet edges at ~15 m height; PV roof reached only via steel ladder (p.8); MS fabrication under customer scope; lifting past chajjas and near overhead wires (p.5).
verdicts.rationale: Overhanging modules at height with ladder-only access suggest cleaning/maintenance challenges; 'No' is questionable but not a clear contradiction.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Access to PV roof is by a steep steel ladder from the lower terrace (p.8); installation work is along parapet tops at the roof edge (pp. 11-13) of a ~15 m building; overhead conductors near the facade (p.5).
verdicts.rationale: Edge work and ladder access are visible safety considerations; recommend reviewer confirm 'No' or add fall-protection notes.

verdicts.rationale: Route is wall-mounted end to end; no trench indicated.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run - from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel - with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target - the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: DC (red/green) runs along parapet tops (p.12) and down the side wall (p.13) to the utility room window (p.17) and into the inverter (pp. 14, 21). AC (purple) from inverter down external wall/pipes (p.14 bottom, p.15 top), through wall hole (p.15 bottom) to meter room (p.16) and into meter cubicle (p.21). Earthing (green) continues down the building (p.17-18) to AC/DC pits (p.22); LA (orange) from headroom (p.19) down (p.20) to LA pit (p.22). Pages 15 bottom and 16 top are badly blurred. No conduit/clipping details are shown - routes are drawn lines only.
verdicts.rationale: Routes are traceable and continuous with no orphan ends, but conduit/clamp details are absent and two key photos near the meter room are blurred, so the exposed-run protection cannot be confirmed.
